subject: Reasoning
topic: Mathematical Operations — Custom Symbol Definitions and Expression Evaluation (W13 B1)

questions.stem: If A @ B = A + B − 3, find the value of 5 @ 4.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A@B = A+B−3. Substitute A=5, B=4: 5+4−3=6. Trap: 9 = only A+B (forgetting to subtract 3); 3 = only B−A (wrong formula reading); 5 = A alone.

questions.stem: If A # B = 2A − B, find the value of 4 # 3.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A#B = 2A−B. Substitute A=4, B=3: 2×4−3=8−3=5. Trap: 8 = 2A only (forgot to subtract B); 5 reverified: 8−3=5 ✓; 3 = only B (ignores 2A entirely).

questions.stem: If A ★ B = A × B + A, find the value of 2 ★ 3.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A★B = A×B+A = A(B+1). Substitute A=2, B=3: 2×3+2=6+2=8. Alternatively: A(B+1)=2×4=8 ✓. Trap: 6 = A×B only (forgot the +A part); 9 = (A+B)×... some wrong formula.

questions.stem: If A $ B = (A − B)², find the value of 7 $ 3.
questions.explanation: B is correct. A$B=(A−B)². 7$3=(7−3)²=4²=16. Trap: 10 = just A−B+? some wrong reading; 49 = A² (ignores the subtraction of B); 28 = maybe (A−B)×A or wrong computation.

questions.stem: If A @ B = A + B − 3, find (3 @ 4) @ 5.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Step 1: 3@4 = 3+4−3=4. Step 2: 4@5 = 4+5−3=6. Final answer=6. This is a chained operation question. Trap: 9 = adds all three (3+4+5=12 then−3=9, applies formula only once); 7 = 3+4+5−5=7 (wrong).

questions.stem: If A % B = A² − B², find the value of 5 % 4.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A%B = A²−B². 5%4=5²−4²=25−16=9. SHORTCUT: A²−B²=(A+B)(A−B)=(5+4)(5−4)=9×1=9 ✓. Trap: 41 = 5²+4² (adds instead of subtracts); 1 = A−B (linear, not quadratic); 3 = some other wrong operation.

questions.stem: If A ★ B = AB/(A+B), find the value of 6 ★ 3.
questions.explanation: B is correct. A★B=AB/(A+B). 6★3=(6×3)/(6+3)=18/9=2. This formula appears in combined-rate problems (e.g., harmonic mean of rates). Trap: 3 = A/B=6/3=2? No — 6÷3=2 is B, not the formula; 9 = A+B=9 (numerator only, forgot denominator).

questions.stem: If A ⊕ B = (A+B)² − A² − B², find the value of 4 ⊕ 3.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A⊕B=(A+B)²−A²−B². Expand: A²+2AB+B²−A²−B²=2AB. So A⊕B=2AB. 4⊕3=2×4×3=24. SHORTCUT: recognise the algebraic identity (A+B)²−A²−B²=2AB. Students who expand get: (4+3)²−4²−3²=49−16−9=24 ✓. Students who know the identity get it instantly. This is a classic paper-setter shortcut trap. Trap: 14 = 2(A+B)=14 (wrong); 49 = (A+B)² only (forgot subtraction).

questions.stem: If '+' means '×', '×' means '−', '−' means '+', '÷' means '÷', what is the value of 6 + 2 × 3 − 4 ÷ 2?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Step 1 — substitute operators in the expression '6+2×3−4÷2': '+' becomes '×': 6×2; '×' becomes '−': 2−3; '−' becomes '+': 3+4; '÷' stays '÷': 4÷2. New expression: 6×2−3+4÷2. Step 2 — apply BODMAS on the new expression: ÷ first: 4÷2=2; × next: 6×2=12; then left-to-right: 12−3+2=11. Answer=11. Verify: 12−3=9; 9+2=11 ✓. Trap: 13 = skips BODMAS and goes left-to-right on the ORIGINAL expression before substituting operators; 15 = evaluates ÷ last instead of first.

questions.stem: If A # B = (A+B)(A−B), find the value of (5 # 3) + (4 # 1).
questions.explanation: C is correct. A#B=(A+B)(A−B)=A²−B². 5#3=(5²−3²)=25−9=16. 4#1=(4²−1²)=16−1=15. Sum=16+15=31. SHORTCUT: recognise A#B=A²−B² (difference of squares). Chained evaluation is instant with this identity. Trap: 35 = (5+3)+(4+1)×something; 28 = one of the partial computations.
